questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
Yield the right-of-way.
Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter.
questions.explanation: This sign is placed on one-way streets and roads where you cannot drive. You may see it if you try to go the wrong way on an expressway ramp.

questions.question: If cars pass you on both the right and left while you are in the center lane of an expressway, you should:

options.text: Stay in the center lane.
Move to the right lane.
Move to the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane.
questions.explanation: On roads with four or more lanes, drive in the right lanes unless you are passing or turning left. On interstate highways, use the right lane if you are driving slower than the traffic around you.

questions.question: When you merge onto the freeway, you should drive:

options.text: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
5 to 10 mph slower than freeway traffic.
At the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging onto a freeway, match the speed of traffic around you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No turns.
No outlet.
No U-turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turns.
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed. You may see it at intersections where oncoming traffic is common.

questions.question: Having a driver license is a:

options.text: Requirement.
Privilege.
Right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Privilege.
questions.explanation: Driving is a privilege, not a right. All drivers must help keep roads safe. If you misuse this privilege, it can be taken away.

questions.question: The two-second rule applies when driving at:

options.text: Speeds up to 30 mph.
Any speed.
Speeds up to 55 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any speed.
questions.explanation: The two-second rule works at any speed on highways with normal speed limits. In bad weather, on interstate highways, or at night, increase your distance to at least four seconds.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, return to your original lane when:

options.text: You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
You have cleared the front bumper of the passed vehicle.
You are 50 feet in front of the passed vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Move back into your original lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. This ensures you have enough room to safely pull back in front.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Change lanes in an intersection.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes in an intersection.
questions.explanation: Never change lanes inside an intersection. Always look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Watch for other drivers who may be moving into the same lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Hospital.
Upcoming intersection.
Railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Upcoming intersection.
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to something ahead. They are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that an intersection is coming so you can prepare for traffic or turning.

questions.question: When passing, return to the right lane when:

options.text: You are one vehicle length ahead of the passed vehicle.
You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
You are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Only pass if you have enough space to return to your lane safely. Make sure you have enough distance between you and the vehicle you passed. When you can see both headlights in your rearview mirror, it is safe to return to your lane.

questions.question: You are approaching an intersection with a steady yellow traffic light. If you have not entered the intersection yet, you should:

options.text: Speed up to cross before the red light.
Slow down and proceed carefully through the intersection.
Stop safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection, clear it as quickly as possible.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, you should NOT:

options.text: Continue on the freeway and find another route to your destination.
Go to the next exit, leave the freeway, and return to your correct exit.
Back up on the road or shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Back up on the road or shoulder.
questions.explanation: Never back up on the road or shoulder. Drive to the next exit instead. Other drivers do not expect vehicles to back up, which can cause crashes.

questions.question: Roads are slippery when rain first starts to fall. On a slippery road, you should:

options.text: Avoid making fast turns and stops.
Test your tire grip while going uphill.
Look closer to your vehicle instead of far ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid making fast turns and stops.
questions.explanation: Wet roads reduce tire grip. Drive slower and avoid sudden turns or stops to prevent skidding.

questions.question: If your vehicle's rear is skidding to the left, you should:

options.text: Keep your steering wheel straight.
Turn your steering wheel to the left.
Turn your steering wheel to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel to the left.
questions.explanation: If you skid, take your foot off the gas and brakes. Turn the steering wheel in the direction of the skid. If you have anti-lock brakes, apply them firmly and steer straight.

questions.question: When you approach an intersection with a flashing red traffic signal, you must:

options.text: Stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go.
Slow down and proceed carefully.
Stop completely and stay stopped while the light is red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and go when it is safe.

questions.question: You should always drive at:

options.text: The same speed as the vehicles around you.
The speed limit.
A speed that matches road and weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: A speed that matches road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: Your speed should depend on road conditions, weather, and the legal speed limit. Never drive above the speed limit. Slow down when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: On a green arrow, you must:

options.text: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
Yield to pedestrians only.
Wait four seconds before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go. Turn in the direction the arrow points after you yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection.

questions.question: If another vehicle is passing you in a no passing zone, you should:

options.text: Pull off the road.
Keep your speed and position the same.
Slow down and let the other driver safely return to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the other driver safely return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Help the passing vehicle return to your lane safely so they can avoid hazards ahead.

questions.question: The Implied Consent Law means:

options.text: You agree to take a test for alcohol or drugs if asked.
Traffic laws apply at intersections without signs, markings, or signals.
You do not have to take a test for alcohol or drugs if asked.

questions.correctAnswerText: You agree to take a test for alcohol or drugs if asked.
questions.explanation: The Implied Consent Law means that by driving in Tennessee, you agree to be tested for drugs or alcohol if asked.

questions.question: What does a yellow left arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: Drivers should prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.
The protected left turn is ending.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: A yellow left arrow means the protected turn is ending and you must prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When exiting the interstate, when should you slow down?

options.text: About halfway through the deceleration lane.
As you approach the deceleration lane.
Right when you enter the deceleration lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right when you enter the deceleration lane.
questions.explanation: Keep your speed when leaving the interstate. Slow down as soon as you enter the deceleration lane to match the posted speed for the exit ramp.

questions.question: How far ahead should you signal before turning?

options.text: At least 50 feet.
As soon as you decide to turn.
At least 100 feet.

questions.correctAnswerText: At least 50 feet.
questions.explanation: Turn on your turn signal at least 50 feet before you turn.

questions.question: You drive defensively when you:

options.text: Keep one car length between you and the car ahead.
Look only at the car directly in front of you.
Keep scanning ahead and around for dangers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep scanning ahead and around for dangers.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means looking ahead for possible hazards. Staring only at the road in front of your car is unsafe. Scan ahead and watch for vehicles around you.

questions.question: How should you make room for cars entering the freeway?

options.text: Slow down.
Move to a different lane.
Keep your speed and position the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane.
questions.explanation: Make room for vehicles entering the freeway. Change lanes if you can to create space for them. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to let them merge safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road curves or gets narrower ahead.
No right turn.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves or gets narrower ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road curves or narrows. You will see these signs on sharp curves or near narrow bridges.

questions.question: At an uncontrolled intersection, when you arrive at the same time as vehicles on your left and right, what should you do?

options.text: Yield to the vehicle on your left.
Yield to the vehicle on your right.
Wait until all vehicles are gone before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to the vehicle on your right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no signs or signals, the vehicle on your right has the right-of-way. After that, vehicles go in the order they arrived.

questions.question: A large truck ahead is turning right onto a street with two lanes in each direction. The truck:

options.text: Can finish the turn in either of the two lanes.
May need to swing wide to complete the turn.
Must stay in the right lane while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: May need to swing wide to complete the turn.
questions.explanation: When turning, the rear wheels follow a shorter path than the front wheels. Long trucks need extra space to turn right because the difference between front and rear wheel paths is bigger.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Turn the wheels toward the curb.
Turn the wheels away from the curb.
Leave the wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb. When parking uphill on a street without a curb or parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must stop for other traffic.
Traffic is merging from another road. Give them space to safely merge into traffic.
Traffic is merging from another road. Keep to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is merging from another road. Give them space to safely merge into traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic will merge into your lane. Check your side and rear mirrors. If possible, change lanes to give merging drivers a clear path.

questions.question: Large trucks are most likely to lose speed when:

options.text: Going up long or steep hills.
Going through long, gradual curves.
Going down long, gradual hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Going up long or steep hills.
questions.explanation: Large trucks take longer to speed up than smaller vehicles. They lose speed going up long or steep hills. Give trucks extra space, especially on hills.
